notes.modeling_currency: Model is built in EUR at the ordinary-share level (ADYEN.AS, 31.5m diluted ordinary shares), consistent with Adyen's reporting currency and share structure. ADYEY is a US ADR where 1 ADR = 1/100th of one ordinary share.
notes.conversion_methodology: IV per ADR (USD) = IV per ordinary share (EUR) x EURUSD (1.1446) / 100
notes.ordinary_share_price_check: $9.45 ADR x 100 / 1.1446 = EUR 825.9, consistent with ADYEN.AS trading around EUR 833.10 on 2026-07-18
notes.net_cash_derivation: Gross balance-sheet cash of EUR 10,797.4m is inflated by merchant settlement funds and is NOT available for equity holders. Own-cash = Cash (10,797.4) - Payables to merchants (6,371.8) + Receivables from merchants/FI (561.7) = EUR 4,987.3m. Net cash = Own-cash - Lease liabilities (252.4) = EUR 4,734.9m. This net cash figure (as a negative net_debt) is used in the DCF bridge.
notes.fcf_definition: FCF = EBITDA - CapEx (Adyen does not report unlevered FCF directly; conversion has been ~85-87% of EBITDA and stable). FY2025 FCF = EUR 1,081.3m, +25.8% YoY, EBITDA margin 52.7%, FCF/EBITDA conversion 86.8%.
notes.fy2025_not_peak: FY2025 FCF is NOT a cyclical peak - Adyen guided FY2026 net revenue growth of 20-22% CC with EBITDA margin roughly flat to FY2025 (~53%) and capex <=5% of net revenue, implying continued double-digit FCF growth into FY2026 and beyond.

inputs.shares_outstanding_note: millions of ordinary shares (diluted), FY2025. ADR count = shares_outstanding x 100 = 3,150m ADRs equivalent.
inputs.net_debt_note: Negative = net cash position of EUR 4,734.9m (own-cash basis, see notes.net_cash_derivation)
inputs.units: millions (per ordinary share EUR; per ADR figures converted to USD)
inputs.fx_note: TODO: filing currency differs from the quote currency. Record the rate used, its date, its source, and a parity check (a dual listing if one exists), and confirm the canonical intrinsic_value / weighted_iv are stated in the QUOTE currency so they are comparable to current_price.

historical_growth.eps_note: EPS CAGR omitted as an anchor; net-revenue and FCF CAGRs are more meaningful for a payments platform with growing embedded-finance/interest-income mix
historical_growth.growth_rate_source: revenue_3yr_cagr (net revenue), cross-checked against fcf_3yr_cagr (21.2%) and FY2026 guidance (20-22% CC)
historical_growth.growth_divergence_warning: Shareholders'-equity CAGR (~30% 3yr / ~34% 5yr) is materially higher than net-revenue CAGR (~21% 3yr / ~28% 5yr) and FCF CAGR (~21% 3yr / ~26% 5yr). This divergence is an artifact of 100% earnings retention (Adyen pays no dividends and conducts no buybacks), not superior underlying economics. Net-revenue CAGR (~21%) is used as the primary anchor for FY2026 base-case growth, consistent with management's own 20-22% CC guidance and Q1-2026 actual (+20% CC).

base.growth_rate_basis: FCF growth. Starts at FY2026 guidance midpoint (20-22% CC net revenue growth, roughly flat EBITDA margin -> FCF grows in line), decelerates ~2-3pp/yr toward terminal growth over the 5-year window.
base.fcf_margin: n/a - FCF projected directly via growth rate off FY2025 base of EUR 1,081.3m rather than via a revenue x margin build, consistent with company FCF-conversion stability (~85-87% of EBITDA)

bull.growth_rate_basis: Growth holds in the low-to-mid 20s: Platforms pillar +50% continues to scale, North America execution improves, EBITDA margin expansion to 55-58% pulled forward toward 2028 target aids FCF conversion, Talon.One/Orb cross-sell contributes.

bear.growth_rate_basis: Growth steps down to low-to-mid teens: Stripe/Checkout.com competitive pressure intensifies, take-rate compression resumes, enterprise mix shift weighs on blended growth, margin stays flat (no further FCF conversion improvement), leadership-transition disruption (CFO departure, Co-CEO health step-back) weighs on execution.

sensitivity.note: Values are intrinsic value per ADR (USD), base-case FCF growth path (20/17/15/13/11.5%)

sanity_check.diagnosis: No fix needed. Base-case IV ($10.70/ADR = ~€935/ordinary share) implies 27.7x trailing P/E and 19.8x EV/EBITDA — BELOW the cheapest FY-end multiples in Adyen's public history (40.8x P/E, 31.0x EV/EBITDA at end-2025). The stock has de-rated continuously since IPO (P/E 111x in 2018 -> 41x in 2025 -> ~25x today at $9.45); the DCF assumes no re-rating, only cash-flow growth. Note the historical averages are hypergrowth-era multiples and are NOT evidence the market will pay them again; the check is one-directional (it guards against over-valuation) and the model sits comfortably on the conservative side.
sanity_check.context: Current price $9.45 is at the LOWEST valuation multiple in the company's history despite FY2025 net revenue +21% CC and EBITDA +26%. Base case upside is a modest +13.2%, driven by cash-flow growth assumptions in line with company guidance (20-22% CC for 2026), not by multiple expansion.
